title: PulseTech: code, derived data and supporting information for a human-in-the-loop web dashboard for pediatric FAERS pharmacovigilance with heterogeneous graph neural network signal exploration
description:
Code, derived datasets, supplementary tables and figures accompanying the manuscript PulseTech: Design and implementation of a human-in-the-loop web dashboard for pediatric FAERS pharmacovigilance with heterogeneous graph neural network signal exploration, submitted to PLOS ONE.

Contents: complete signal-detection results for 6,259 drug–ADR pairs in four ICH E11(R1) pediatric age bands from the Q1 2025 signal cache, with the counts from which every statistic can be recomputed (S8 Table); the database exports from which the reported counts were taken, with two scripts that re-check those counts and the signal flags; graph-construction, HANConv model, link-ranking, signal-flagging, pipeline and validation scripts; the held-out link-prediction evaluation script with its per-seed results; a script comparing the signals with drug labels (SIDER 4.1, not redistributed) with its aggregate output; figure sources; and S1–S10 Tables.

Primary data: FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), 2021Q1–2025Q4, publicly available from the U.S. FDA. MedDRA is licensed from the MSSO and no MedDRA dictionary files are redistributed. Licences: source code MIT; data, tables, figures and documents CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE and DATA_LICENSE.md). See README.md for the reproducibility status and known issues of this version.
